newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador studying debt restructuring-gov't official.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador studying debt restructuring-gov't official.

text.p: Ecuador is studying restructuring its foreign debt to ease interest payments, a top government official said Tuesday.
Public Credit Under Secretary Ernesto Perez told Reuters in an interview that the plan will be announced in 15 days.
Perez said that the government is concentrating its attention on restructuring its Paris Club debt, which will total $1.1 billion by the end of 1997.
He said the government aims to meet its overdue payments due with the Paris Club, which will total about $380 million in capital and interest by the end of the year.
While Ecuador is seeking to pay overdue interest, Perez said that Japan and some U.S. agencies are pressing for higher payments before any Paris Club restructuring.
"But some agencies are also willing to make donations to the country. They have asked us to try and put our payments up to date and that's the line that Germany and France are taking," he said.
Ecuador recently issued $250 million in bonds, using $190 million to refinance internal debt and $20 million to pay overdue interest with the Paris Club.
